acceptance_criteria.criterion: The sanitiser exists as committed, versioned code and is called by a committed recorder, replacing the throwaway script each session used to write and delete
The same logical path sanitises to identical bytes regardless of separator style, case on Windows-shaped prefixes, or a bare drive root -- while POSIX case-distinct directories are NOT conflated
A prefix match requires a path boundary, so a sibling directory sharing the repo's prefix is not corrupted
Each command records the sanitiser_version that produced its digest, a verifiable flag, a reason from a closed enum when false, and resolved shas when its argv names a git range

On a pull_request run, where CI holds a genuinely external PR number, every proof record new or changed in the range must declare that number regardless of its filename -- closing both the slug-named and self-consistent-filename bypasses
Where no external number exists, the output states that every pr field is self-declared and unverified rather than implying a check occurred
This record is the first in the repo produced by the committed recorder rather than a script that deleted itself

tokens.source: transcript message.usage summed across this session's usage-bearing assistant records. Covers the WHOLE session across PRs 12-20 and EXCLUDES all subagent spend -- this PR alone ran four review passes and five implementer rounds. A floor, not a total.

unproven: 3 OF 8 COMMANDS IN THIS RECORD ARE INDEPENDENTLY RE-EXECUTABLE, as the recorder itself reports. That is not the repo-wide figure: five of ten distinct command KINDS are re-executable across all records. This record omits lwb_check_proof.py and its --pr form deliberately -- a record cannot contain proof of its own existence, and including them would make CI re-execution recurse into itself.

NO DIGEST IN THIS REPO HAS EVER BEEN COMPARED TO ANYTHING. This PR makes a digest ATTRIBUTABLE to versioned code; the CI job that re-executes verifiable commands and compares digests does not exist yet and is the next PR. Until it runs, every sha256 here is a number nobody has checked.

Records 7-19 predate the sanitiser-as-code and are NOT back-filled. Their digests were produced by per-session throwaway scripts that disagreed about their own substitutions, so none is independently reproducible. A back-filled digest would be a fabricated receipt.

Whether github.event.pull_request.base.sha and head.sha resolve as expected in a live Actions run is UNVERIFIED. No reviewer executed one; PyYAML is not installed here to parse-validate the workflow. This PR's own CI run is the experiment.
On a local run or a push to main there is no external PR number, so only the filename cross-check runs -- which catches an inconsistent lie, not a self-consistent one. The runtime output says so.

The bare two-revision form (git diff origin/main HEAD) is not detected as a range; a well-formed but nonexistent sha passes the resolved_* pattern; and the recorder has no timeout, so a hung command hangs it. Each is named in code with a pinning test where one applies.
checked_by is a subagent of the author's session and declares reviewer_was_dispatched_by_author: true. This is an audit trail, not proof of independent review.
This record was written by the author of the work it proves.

CORRECTED 2026-09-19 (found by independent review of a LATER PR): the 'python scripts/lwb_handoff.py --check' command above was originally marked verifiable: true. It is not. That command's own output prints the byte count of HANDOFF.md's GENERATED block, which legitimately changes with live repo state (main SHA, open-PR listing, the proof-state summary) independent of any change to tracked content -- observed printing 2262 bytes on main (f8cb770) and 2214 bytes on a feature branch (107d5f4) with the file itself unchanged. Its digest can therefore only reproduce when the byte count happens to coincide across commits, which is a coincidence, not reproducibility. verifiable is now false with reason nondeterministic-output (the closest honest enum value; none names 'embeds a generated-block byte count' directly). Only the verifiable/verifiable_reason flags and this note changed -- argv, exit, tail, and sha256 for that command are byte-for-byte identical to what PR #20 originally shipped; rewriting captured evidence, rather than correcting the author's own classification of it, would be the fabrication this record format exists to prevent.
